questions.stem: For each antiemetic, indicate the adverse effects the nurse should watch for. Each row may have more than one answer.

rationale.correct: Antiemetics have predictable effects: serotonin antagonists and phenothiazines prolong QT; dopamine antagonists cause EPS; steroids raise glucose.

exhibits.title: Oncology orders
exhibits.body: Hold citalopram today. Cardiac monitoring. Recheck electrolytes in 6 hours.

questions.stem: Potassium chloride 40 mEq in 250 mL 0.9% sodium chloride is prescribed to run at 10 mEq/hour through a peripheral line. At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Record your answer as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 40 mEq / 250 mL = 0.16 mEq/mL. 10 mEq/hour / 0.16 mEq/mL = 62.5 mL/hour, about 63 mL/hour, over 4 hours. Potassium is never given by IV push.

questions.stem: Before the next cycle, the client describes the plan for nausea. For each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll take the antiemetics on schedule for 3 days, even if I feel fine."
"I'll eat small, bland meals and avoid strong smells."
"I'll call if I can't keep fluids down for 24 hours."
"I'll wait until I'm sick before taking anything."
"If my legs feel restless, I'll take extra metoclopramide."
"I'll drink 2 to 3 liters a day to protect my kidneys."

rationale.correct: Scheduled prevention, diet changes and early reporting prevent delayed CINV complications.

questions.stem: The paracentesis fluid shows 480 neutrophils/mm3. Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: This result means {{b1}}. The client is at risk for {{b2}} because of {{b3}}.

options.text: infection and rising creatinine in cirrhosis

rationale.correct: SBP is diagnosed by ascitic neutrophils; it commonly leads to hepatorenal syndrome.

perOption.b1:a: 250 or more neutrophils/mm3 in ascitic fluid.
perOption.b1:d: Would show many organisms and other findings.
perOption.b2:a: SBP often triggers kidney failure in cirrhosis.
perOption.b3:a: Circulatory changes reduce kidney blood flow.
perOption.b3:c: Can contribute to low pressure, but infection is the main trigger.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily. Albumin 1.5 g/kg day 1 and 1 g/kg day 3. Hold diuretics. Therapeutic paracentesis of 5 L with albumin.

questions.stem: During the 5 L paracentesis, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Have the client empty the bladder before the procedure
Position the client upright or semi-Fowler's
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate during and after
Give albumin as prescribed after the drainage
Check the site for leaking fluid
Drain as quickly as possible to shorten the procedure

rationale.correct: Safe paracentesis: empty bladder, upright position, monitoring, albumin and site checks.

perOption.b: Fluid pools in the lower abdomen.
perOption.f: Rapid removal without albumin risks hypotension.

exhibits.body: Transfuse 2 units packed red cells. Four-factor PCC 50 units/kg. CT angiography. GI and interventional radiology consults.

questions.stem: Fifteen minutes into the first unit, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the line open with 0.9% sodium chloride through new tubing
Notify the provider and blood bank
Send the blood bag, tubing and a blood and urine sample as policy requires
Slow the transfusion and give acetaminophen
Recheck the label and restart if it matches

rationale.correct: Fever, back pain and falling pressure during a transfusion mean stopping it and starting the reaction protocol.

perOption.b: Keeps access without giving more blood.
perOption.e: Back pain with fever and hypotension is not a minor reaction.

exhibits.title: Oncology unit, day 2 after cisplatin
exhibits.body: A 52-year-old client received cisplatin for head and neck cancer yesterday. Antiemetics: ondansetron 8 mg every 8 hours, dexamethasone and aprepitant on day 1. Since this morning the client has vomited 7 times and cannot keep fluids down. The client also takes citalopram and was given metoclopramide 10 mg IV twice overnight. The client now has restlessness and cannot sit still.

caseStudies.title: Ascites, paracentesis and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis

exhibits.title: Medical unit
exhibits.body: A 57-year-old client with cirrhosis has a tense, distended abdomen and shortness of breath when lying flat. The client has mild abdominal tenderness and a temperature of 38.1 C (100.6 F). Medicines: spironolactone 100 mg and furosemide 40 mg daily, propranolol. Weight 82 kg (74 kg a month ago).

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 1900
exhibits.body: A 79-year-old client with atrial fibrillation takes apixaban 5 mg twice daily (last dose at 0800) and aspirin 81 mg. Since this afternoon the client has passed large amounts of bright red and maroon blood from the rectum four times and feels faint. History of diverticulosis.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 64-year-old client has had left lower abdominal pain for 3 days, fever and constipation. The left lower abdomen is tender with guarding. The client eats little fiber. CT: sigmoid diverticulitis with a 5 cm abscess.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
